source.title: Merengue 2
source.scope: Author's retrospective observation from Santo Domingo, published with a 2003 time reference. Describes conga accompaniment when tambora is present, expressly uncertain whether it is traditional. No named performance, player or merengue subtype is identified.
source.verification: Complete two-row notation and linked stroke key visually inspected. One reader; independent player audit pending.

rights: Basic rhythmic cells studied from the publicly supplied author's lesson. No notation image, prose, recording or sample is embedded in the machine. Release 727 adaptation; no endorsement is asserted.

adaptation.note: S=slap, B=bass stroke on the conga, O=open. Preserve onsets and the lower drum on beat four of bar one. The 727 has no conga bass stroke: map it to unaccented mute high conga, with accented mute high conga for slap. Accents are Compas choices, not printed dynamics. This is a conga part to accompany tambora, not a whole merengue ensemble or a bass-guitar line.
